title: Personal data is in every commit tree, and the window to rewrite closes at publication
evidence: the personal profile and .claude/settings.json both introduced in cfb6988, the initial commit
both live at HEAD, so present in all 21 trees

notes: Deleting at HEAD leaves the blobs readable at 21 commit URLs forever. One author, one branch, no tags, no PR history, so rm -rf .git plus a single initial commit — or git filter-repo --invert-paths over those two files — is cheap now and impossible later. Do not rewrite the author identity: commit authorship under a public GitHub account is public by construction. Owner's decision; the reproducibility lens judged a rewrite unwarranted and that read is legitimate. FIXED: rewritten to a single root commit before the repo was ever public. The findings layer itself turned out to be the largest remaining leak — it quoted the profile's name field, the home FIPS and an email that appeared nowhere else in the tree. Scrubbed into the same root commit rather than a follow-up, since a fix committed on top would have left the leaking blob in the root and defeated the rewrite. Anything asserting the tree is clean must include docs/data in its grep; the early sweeps excluded it.

title: The published artifact, not the repo, is the redistribution surface — and it carries CHR&R data
evidence: the repo vendors no upstream data: git grep finds only URLs, and data/cache/.gitkeep is the sole tracked file under data/
builder.py:31-41 embeds dataset.to_dict() plus county paths, state paths, centroids, city markers and city metrics into out/refugia.html
five of the six specs draw on County Health Rankings, whose content is all-rights-reserved under a personal/non-profit-only licence
template.html:2678-2679 builds the credit line from registered metrics only
notes: Publishing the code is unaffected by any upstream terms — the repo ships URLs, not data, and each user fetches under their own licence. The obligation attaches to the generated page, which embeds CHR&R-derived values for ~1,900 counties and geometry derived from ISC-licensed us-atlas. Consequences: the page must carry the CHR&R citation, the Zillow attribution and the us-atlas ISC notice (fnd-009); a GitHub Pages demo (fnd-034) is the owner redistributing CHR&R content and needs those credits in place first; and the README should tell users a page they share carries the same obligations. Commercial use of a shared page needs CHR&R's prior written consent, so a non-commercial framing (fnd-026) is worth stating deliberately rather than by omission.

title: County Health Rankings is non-commercial-only, which constrains what refugia may become
evidence: countyhealthrankings.org/terms-use — licence is 'for personal or non-profit purposes including educational, research, or public health'
same page — content 'may not be copied or otherwise used for commercial use ... without CHR&R's express prior written consent'
all content 'is the property of CHR&R or its licensors with all rights reserved' — not public domain
five of six specs: air_pollution, life_expectancy, poor_mental_health_days, poor_or_fair_health, social_associations
notes: The binding constraint on the whole project, and the only source that is not freely licensed. Publishing the code is unaffected — the repo ships URLs, not data. What it forecloses is a commercial form: a hosted service, a paid tier, or anything sold on top of a page carrying these five metrics needs CHR&R's prior written consent. Discussion needed on whether to state a non-commercial position explicitly, drop to the federal sources underneath the CHR&R compilation (their analytic file is the licensed thing, not the underlying facts), or ask CHR&R for written consent. Doing nothing is defensible for a personal project and is the current de facto position.
review_at: before any hosted, paid or commercial form of refugia
